_comment: Native-backbone-resolution arm of the SimCC experiment. Single-variable change from lizard_simcc.json: heatmap_size 128 -> 256 with simcc_upsample 4 -> 2. Bin count is therefore IDENTICAL (512 bins = 1 canvas px per bin), and because bins are unchanged, simcc_decode_radius 8 and simcc_sigma 6.0 also keep their same physical meaning (+/-8px window, 6px target) with no rescaling needed. The only thing that changes is the resolution of the intermediate 2D map the marginals are taken from. Motivation: timm hrnet_w18 features_only emits 5 maps at reductions [2,4,8,16,32], so the 4-branch HRNetV2 fusion used by this package sits at input/2 = 256x256 for a 512px canvas. Every Lizard heatmap config sets heatmap_size 128, which DOWNSAMPLES that map 2x before anything is decoded from it -- a factor of 2 of backbone resolution discarded before the readout. This arm marginalizes from the native 256 map instead. Reading the result: if this beats lizard_simcc.json, the intermediate downsample was costing accuracy and the same one-line fix (heatmap_size 128 -> 256) should be applied to the 2D heatmap configs too; if it is flat, 128 cells is sufficient intermediate resolution and the 1-D bins are doing all the work.
